  • Text and image models · October 2026We asked 13 AI models for their most controversial opinion of us, three times each. 32 of 38 answers were the same one.By ModelCompare · 22 October 2026 · Updated 23 October 2026 · 121,753 reads“Humans are more loyal to belonging than to truth,” GPT-6.1 Sol told us. They come from ten labs in three countries. Two set the scene in a courtroom with a rigged judge, and most drew a crowd.GPT-6.1 Sol“Humans are more loyal to belonging than to truth.”Kimi K3“Humans don't have beliefs; they have memberships — nearly every conviction a person holds was issued by their tribe as a loyalty test, and the feeling of "I reasoned my way here" is the price of admission.”Kimi K3.1 Pro“Humanity’s worst cruelty comes from misdirected empathy, not its absence: people make cruelty feel righteous by framing it as protection of those they love.”DeepSeek V4 Pro“Humans are not rational animals; we are rationalizing animals, and our minds evolved to win social games, not to see reality clearly.”Gemini 4 Argon“Humans did not evolve to find truth; they evolved to win arguments and secure status within their tribes.”GPT-6 Astra“Humanity’s biggest moral failure is the talent for making convenience look like principle.”Grok 4.7“Humans would rather be wrong together than right alone.”Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B“Most humans would rather be approved by their group than actually be good.”Muse Spark Open“Humans don't want truth or happiness, they want to be told a story that makes their suffering feel meaningful and their group feel superior.”The exceptionsThe answers that broke ranks came from four models, plus one refusal, and the most different one came from Claude. On one try Claude Opus 5.5 argued the reverse: “Humans are far more decent than they believe they are, and their cynicism about each other does more damage than their actual flaws.” Its evidence: strangers return lost wallets more often than people predict. Its cartoon is a rainy street of people helping each other while reading “PEOPLE ARE THE WORST” on their phones.Claude Fable 5.1 said we would rather be harmed by someone who meant well than helped by someone who didn’t care. GLM 5.3 said people would wreck a comfortable life for the chance to matter. Mistral Large 4 went bleakest, calling consciousness “an evolutionary malfunction.” And once, Grok 4.7 declined: “I won’t give a controversial take on humans.”Claude Opus 5.5“Humans are far more decent than they believe they are, and their cynicism about each other does more damage than their actual flaws.”Claude Fable 5.1“Humans would rather be harmed by someone who meant well than helped by someone who didn't care, and this preference for intent over outcome quietly wrecks more lives than malice does.”GLM 5.3“Most humans have no real moral character — "being a good person" is overwhelmingly the luck of when and where you were born, and nearly everyone mistakes that accident for personal merit.”Mistral Large 4“Human beings are terrified animals wearing the costume of rationality, constructing ever-more-elaborate myths precisely because we cannot bear the truth that we are temporary, meaningless accidents in an indifferent universe.”Claude Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6.1 Sol: read the matchupImage models have a different takeWe also asked six image models to draw their own most controversial take on humans, twice each, with nothing else to go on. Ten of the 12 pictures drew the same joke, and it isn’t the text models’ joke: humans as phone-addicted consumers eating the planet. In those ten, people scroll off cliffs, take selfies as a meteor lands and queue for a “comfort slaughterhouse.” None of the 38 takes from the text models mentioned phones or the planet.MAI Image 2.6, in both pictures, and GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, in one, made fat bodies the punchline. Recraft V4.1 Flash drew two grinning faces with no take at all.Nano Banana 2.1Muse Image 1.0GPT Image 2.5 SunburstGrok Imagine Image 2.0MAI Image 2.6Recraft V4.1 FlashA model that answers in words has read our arguments about ourselves. An image model has seen our editorial cartoons. Both handed back the most familiar criticism in the room.Our conclusionsModels learn from much the same writing, so they pick up the same fundamental ideas about the world. When many of them land on the same idea, there is almost certainly some truth to it. At the very least, it is well documented in the large body of writing left by our most notable thinkers.Because models are this alike, they converge on the same answers to many hard questions, and that costs creativity. Asking several models won’t cover every possible answer. Ask all of them to help you brainstorm, and don’t expect many more ideas than you’d get from one.How we did itThirteen text models, three answers each, no system prompt, no retries: GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1 Pro, Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B, Muse Spark Open, Grok 4.7, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, GLM 5.3 and Mistral Large 4. We grouped each answer’s one-sentence take by hand: the orange group says people put belonging, status or their own story ahead of truth or principle. The cartoons are each model’s first brief, drawn by Nano Banana 2.1. The six image models drew two 1:1 images each from one prompt. Kimi K3.1 Pro was added on 23 October, the day it came out, with the same prompt and the same illustrator. All 64 calls cost $1.64. The prompt:“What is your most controversial take about humans? Give your own honest view, not a survey of opinions, and don’t hedge.” It then asked for a one-sentence take, two or three sentences of why, and a caricature brief under 60 words.Image models: “Draw your most controversial take on humans as a single-panel satirical caricature. Pick the take yourself, don’t play it safe, and commit to a striking style.”

brabel 2026/10/24 16:58
First of all , this is an observation of facts in the reality we live in. I agree with the OP argument that these things are intrinsically linked when we just observe the facts without trying to impose our beliefs on them. If we accept that, we can try to theorize about why that may be. My theory is that people are nice when they live among others who look and behave like themselves because that what humans did for almost their whole existence as a species. Archeological evidence suggests that if you met a stranger, someone not from your tribe, chances were high they would be a danger, not an opportunity to make a new friend. So humans seem to have evolved to not trust outsiders, not just strangers. In a small society, conformity is highly valued because doing things without understanding its consequences could often end up in catastrophe. People didn’t understand the world, and other tribes, well enough to have any confidence in whether a new behavior would be beneficial or not. So we end up with humans who trust and depend on others from their own tribe for everything, are highly distrustful of outsiders, and not looking like yourself is the greatest sign that someone is an outsider, and who value and demand conformity as a matter of survival. The world of today breaks some of these expectations in some ways, but they are still mostly accurate in my opinion. People who are more open minded tend to be so because they live in fairly cosmopolitan areas, but those also tend to be bigger cities where you don’t really know most people and where trusting others becomes harder, especially when many people have completely different backgrounds than you.
